name: Kazakh Khanate
summary: A nomadic state on the Central Asian steppe, founded around 1465 by Kerei and Janibek, who broke away from the Uzbek Khanate. It split into three hordes (zhuz) and came under Russian rule step by step until 1847.

knownFor.label: Yurt
knownFor.note: A portable round felt house that could be packed onto camels and horses.

knownFor.label: Three zhuz (hordes)
knownFor.note: The Senior, Middle and Junior hordes that organised Kazakh tribes.

knownFor.label: Dombra
knownFor.note: A two-stringed lute used to play epic songs and kuy melodies.

location.value: The steppes of present-day Kazakhstan, from the Caspian Sea to the Altai Mountains.

terrain.value: Flat grassland, semi-desert and some mountains in the south-east.

climate.value: Very continental: hot summers and very cold winters.

resources.value: Grazing for horses, sheep and camels; salt; trade cities on the Syr Darya.

disasters.value: Zhut: winters when ice covered the grass and animals starved.

population.value: Perhaps about 1 million people in the 16th century.

urbanisation.value: Mostly nomadic; a few oasis towns such as Turkistan and Sayram.

migration.value: Seasonal migration between summer and winter pastures; Kazakhs fled west during Dzungar invasions (the “Great Disaster”, 1723).

economicBase.value: Pastoral nomadism: herding horses, sheep, goats and camels.

tradeRoutes.value: Traded animals with Bukhara, Khiva and Russian frontier towns for grain, cloth and metal goods.

moneyAndTax.value: Tribute and gifts to khans and sultans; no coinage of its own.

inequality.value: Descendants of Genghis Khan (the “white bone”) ranked above commoners (the “black bone”).

governmentType.value: A khanate led by Genghisid khans, with tribal chiefs (biys) and assemblies.

keyRulers.value: Kerei and Janibek (founders). Kasym Khan (1511–1521). Tauke Khan (law code, about 1680–1715). Ablai Khan (1771–1781). Kenesary Kasymov (revolt, 1837–1847).

succession.value: Khans were chosen from Genghisid families by the leaders of the tribes.

institutions.value: Customary law (adat); Tauke Khan’s code “Zheti Zhargy” (the Seven Charters).

stability.value: Often divided into rival hordes, each with its own khan.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between sultans of different Genghisid lines.

armyAndTech.value: Mounted archers; later firearms bought from Russia and Central Asia.

majorWars.value: Long wars against the Dzungar (Oirat) Khanate (1643–1756), including the Battle of Anrakay (about 1729).

territoryChange.value: Russia absorbed the Junior (1731), Middle and Senior hordes gradually, abolishing the khans by 1847.

alliancesRivals.value: Sought Russian protection against the Dzungars; relations with Qing China after 1757.

scienceEducation.value: Oral epics and poetry passed on by singers (akyn and zhyrau).

openness.value: Open trade with neighbours; a mobile, tribal society.

communicationTransport.value: Horses and camels; whole camps moved with the seasons.

religion.value: Sunni Islam mixed with older steppe beliefs (Tengrism, shamans).

languageWriting.value: Kazakh, a Turkic language; Chagatai Turkic or Persian in writing.

artsArchitecture.value: Epic poetry, felt carpets, decorated harness and jewellery; the Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi in Turkistan.

socialStructure.value: Clans and tribes grouped into three hordes; khans and sultans above commoners.

sharedIdentity.value: Kazakh identity formed through the shared hordes, language and epics.

dailyLife.value: Felt yurts; meat, milk, kumis and cheese (kurt).

neighbours.value: The Dzungars, Uzbek khanates, Siberian Khanate, the Nogai Horde, Russia and Qing China.

colonisation.value: Absorbed into the Russian Empire; Russian forts and settlers followed.

riseSignals.value: The breakaway from Abu’l-Khayr’s Uzbek Khanate attracted many tribes to Kerei and Janibek.

peakPeriod.value: Strongest under Kasym Khan in the early 16th century.

declineSignals.value: Divisions between the hordes and the Dzungar invasions weakened it.

outcome.value: Annexed by the Russian Empire after the defeat of Kenesary’s revolt (1847).

sources.value: Wikipedia: Kazakh Khanate; Olcott, The Kazakhs (1995).

overallCertainty.value: The founding date and many events are known mainly from later chronicles and are approximate.
